'''Peanut butter and jelly sandwiches''', also know as '''PB&Js''', are a type of [[Cookbook:Sandwiches|sandwich]]. They are very quickly made and only require a couple of common ingredients. This makes them quite popular, especially in the [[:Category:American recipes|United States]]. This recipe will detail how to make the most simple, and indeed traditional form of these sandwiches—feel free to add any ingredients that you think would go well.

==Ingredients==
* 2 slices of [[Cookbook:White Bread|white bread]]
* [[Cookbook:Peanut Butter|Peanut butter]]
* [[Cookbook:Jelly|Jelly]] or [[Cookbook:Jam|jam]]

==Procedure==
#Using a spreading knife, spread an even coat of peanut butter on one side of each slice of bread.
#When the bread is evenly covered, spread an even coat of jelly atop the peanut butter.
#After applying the jelly, put one of the slices on a plate (jelly side up) and place the other slice on top of the first (jelly side down).

==Notes, tips, and variations==
* Butter either side of the sandwich with [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]] or [[Cookbook:Margarine|margarine]] before adding peanut butter and jelly.
* Instead of white bread, you can use whole-grain bread, or really any type of bread. Go nuts.
* Try adding in some sliced [[Cookbook:Banana|bananas]]—they go very well with PB&Js.
* If using a [[Cookbook:Crab Apple|crab apple]] jelly, a dash of [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]] will nicely complement the flavours of the sandwich.
* Try adding a bit of [[Cookbook:Honey|honey]], or even entirely substituting it for the jelly.
* Try adding some sweet or savory cream cheese.
* Try [[Cookbook:Toasting|toasting]] the bread before putting the other ingredients on it.
